summary.headline: Bikaji Q2 FY27: snacking value growth ~22% and volume ~15% as Diwali shifted to Q3; gross margin 34.4% hit ~1.7% by price-cost pressure.
summary.overview: Management said Q2 volume growth looked muted because Diwali timing moved demand from Q2 into Q3, with snacking value growth near 22% and volume near 15% versus about 5% overall volume growth. Standalone gross margin was 34.4% in Q2, with about 1.7% hit from input costs, partly offset by a ~3% price increase effective after the September pause. Management guided Q3 as margin-pressured and Q4 as a normalised gross margin with full-year operating margin around 13%. Retail (Chocolate Heaven-type stores, referred to as CHF) grew strongly, with stores added and a 2026 expansion plan.

segments.name: Snacking (ethnic and western)
segments.commentary: Ethnic snacks grew 19.7% and western snacks 44% in Q2, with Bhujia growing ~20% in the second half of Q1 momentum. Management expects snacking growth of about 17%+ over Q2 and Q3 combined.

segments.name: Sweets
segments.commentary: Sweets were negative in Q2 on the Diwali shift; management said Q2+Q3 combined results would look similar to plan.

segments.name: Retail (CHF)
segments.commentary: Retail contributed ~12.6% of company revenue; CHF expected to reach about Rs 160-170 crore in the year (vs ~Rs 100 crore last year), with same-store sales growth of 6-8%.

guidance_outlook: Full-year operating margin currently around 13%; Q3 expected to be margin-pressured given no price increase in September/October.
Q4 expected to show normalised gross margin with exit run-rate above 13% operating margin as the ~3% price increase takes full effect from mid-November.
Focus market growth expected at about 20-23% in second half; company growth to improve with Diwali catch-up in Q3.
Snacking growth targeted at about 17%+ across Q2 and Q3 combined.
No further price increase planned until March unless input costs change; packaging and edible oil prices softening, with pulses expected to benefit from a new crop by December.
Paytm cashback scheme runs September to March; management said no cash cost to company, with ATL spend held at about 2% of sales for the year.
capex_capacity: Bikaner Bhujia production was disrupted in Q1 by Bengal elections; company added a new depot to increase inventory buffer against future disruptions.
Bikaner Bhujia GI tag: product can only be labelled Bikaner Bhujia if made in Bikaner; alternate-location output would not carry the name.
Retail: about 30 stores currently with about 5-6 openings in the last six months; target of about 14 stores by end of year, with a store opened in Stellar in September.
CHF is trying 2,500 sq ft, 700 sq ft and premium experiential formats, including a premium store in Gurgaon.
demand_pricing: Multiple price increases taken across trade channels, with ~3% price correction after September pause; increase effective from around 15 November.
Competition is strong per management, but focus-market share not stated as lost; competitive intensity seen as similar to prior periods.
Five and ten rupee small packs drove volume; company added ~20,000 outlets in the quarter.
Management said modern trade, general trade and all channels showed good demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why is focus-market growth slow and is competition the reason?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the slowdown solely to the Diwali shift and said focus markets outperformed; focus markets are about 25% of business, versus ~12.5% for the total company contribution in the question context.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins improve in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 expected to be under pressure with no September/October price increase; Q4 to be normalised with gross margin rising from price increases taken from November.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sharp price increase in home care and other categories a competitive risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said food and home-care categories are not comparable; price increases for food were taken after gifting packs were produced, with the ~3% move effective from 15 November.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses about 30% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said input cost and fuel and logistics prices rose, and standalone gross margin was hit ~2% vs last quarter; employee cost efficiency partly offset, but advertising spend increased to build momentum.

qa_highlights.question: What is CHF's growth and store plan?
qa_highlights.answer: CHF expects ~Rs 160-170 crore revenue in the year vs ~Rs 100 crore last year, with 6-8% same-store growth, and plans to onboard brand investors next year.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Paytm cashback accounted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cashback is run with Paytm through collectibles and redemptions handled by Paytm, with no cash payout by the company, running September to March.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure in Q3 from input costs with no price increase until November.
Diwali-timing shifts make quarterly comparisons volatile; Q3 catch-up needs to be confirmed.
Focus-market growth needs to reach 20-23% in second half as guided.
Bikaner Bhujia GI-tag positioning if production moves to alternate locations.
Competitive response in snacks and retail (CHF) premium formats.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery and snacking growth, with candid caution on Q3 margin pressure from delayed price increases; guidance on Q4 normalisation is firm but tied to the November price move.
key_quotes: Quarter three will be largely in pressure.
So full year operating margin currently we are close to 13%.

Retail growth 58% in Q2, 64% cumulative as stated
Stated as Q2+Q3 combined last year grew 9%

adds.what: Retail (CHF) stores: about 30 currently, target ~14 more by end of year (~32 store additions cited for FY)
New depot added at Bikaner Bhujia to increase inventory buffer against disruptions

growth.why: Management guides snacking growth of ~17%+ over Q2+Q3 combined, focus-market growth of 20-23% in H2, and full-year operating margin near 13%, backed mainly by a ~3% price increase and Diwali catch-up, with CHF retail targeting Rs 160-170 crore and ~14 stores added by year-end; no capacity additions for the core business were quantified.
